contents.name: Definition 1.2: scalar and vector sub-Gaussian proxy conventions
Lemma 1.3: one-sided Chernoff tails from the sub-Gaussian MGF
contents.reason: The finite-maximum proof derives both scalar tails directly by Markov optimization, then combines them without assuming independence.

contents.name: Lemma 1.4: tail and moment consequences for sub-Gaussian variables
contents.reason: Moment equivalences and tail-to-moment estimates are not needed for the proxy definitions or finite-sample concentration claims commissioned on this page.

contents.name: Lemma 1.5: a converse MGF characterization from sub-Gaussian tails
contents.reason: The page adopts the MGF proxy definition and proves the needed tail consequences locally; this converse characterization adds no prerequisite used by an assigned item.

contents.name: Theorem 1.6: sums of independent sub-Gaussian variables
contents.reason: General sub-Gaussian closure under independent summation is outside the design, which instead commissions bounded-sum and parameterized sub-exponential inequalities.

contents.name: Corollary 1.7: Chernoff bounds for weighted independent sums
contents.reason: The weighted-average concentration application is not used by any assigned statement or example, and its generic Chernoff setup is not needed locally.

contents.name: Lemma 1.8: Hoeffding’s lemma for a centered bounded variable
contents.reason: Its centered bounded-variable MGF estimate is the scalar mechanism underlying the local independent-sum result, which uses the library conditional form.

contents.name: Theorem 1.9: two-sided Hoeffding inequality for independent bounded averages
Lemma 1.10: sub-exponential tail, moment, and MGF estimates
contents.reason: This alternative tail-to-MGF construction is not required because the assigned sub-exponential definition is an explicit restricted-range MGF condition.

contents.name: Definition 1.11: sub-exponential variables with a restricted MGF range
Lemma 1.12: centered squares of sub-Gaussian variables are sub-exponential
contents.reason: Concentration of squared sub-Gaussian variables is a separate application and is neither asserted nor needed by the commissioned sums and maxima.

contents.name: Theorem 1.13: Bernstein inequality for independent sub-exponential variables
Theorem 1.14: finite maxima of sub-Gaussian variables
Lemma 1.15: a linear functional on a polytope maximizes at a vertex
contents.reason: Polytope extreme-point reduction is independent of the Euclidean sphere-net argument and is not used by any assigned concentration item.

contents.name: Theorem 1.16: sub-Gaussian maxima indexed by a finite-vertex polytope
contents.reason: The polytope-indexed maximum is a separate finite-vertex application; the assigned maximum result is stated for arbitrary finite families and sphere nets.

contents.name: Definition 1.17: epsilon-net convention for subsets of Euclidean space
contents.reason: The local lemma states the sphere-net convention and the precise covering inequality used by the vector concentration theorem.

contents.name: Lemma 1.18: volumetric cardinality bound for an epsilon net of the Euclidean ball
contents.reason: The source bounds a ball net, while the local proof establishes the needed sphere version directly by finite Jordan-volume packing and does not rely on its iterative choice step.

contents.name: Theorem 1.19: high-probability control of the sub-Gaussian Euclidean-ball maximum
contents.reason: The local theorem proves the corresponding finite epsilon-net tail estimate for the vector norm, retaining the exact epsilon dependence and handling zero proxy explicitly.

contents.reason: This example explains one route from boundedness to a restricted MGF range; the page defines that range and proves the assigned concentration theorem directly.

contents.name: Definition 4.2: centered sub-exponential variables and restricted MGF parameters
Proposition 4.1.16: one-variable sub-exponential Chernoff tail bound
contents.reason: The independent-sum proof applies the same restricted-range MGF condition and optimizes one common admissible Chernoff parameter.

contents.name: Proposition 4.1.17: tensorization for independent sub-exponential variables
Corollary 4.1.18: tail bound for sums of independent sub-exponential variables
Lemma 4.1.19: a Bernstein-condition MGF bound
contents.reason: The Bernstein moment condition is a distinct hypothesis from the page’s centered restricted-range sub-exponential definition and is not silently identified with it.

contents.name: Proposition 4.1.20: Bennett inequality for independent centered variables
contents.reason: The assigned Bernstein theorem has a direct bounded-variable variance proof with the specified b/3 constant; Bennett’s sharper rate function is not needed.

contents.name: Classical variance-sensitive Bernstein inequality derived immediately after Proposition 4.1.20
contents.reason: The notes explicitly derive the classical Bernstein denominator from the Bennett rate function. The local item proves the bounded-summand MGF route and obtains the sum form and two-sided version directly.

contents.name: Theorem 4.2.3: Azuma–Hoeffding inequality for martingale differences
contents.reason: The local McDiarmid proof constructs its Doob increments and applies the conditional bounded-difference Hoeffding lemma at each step.

contents.name: Corollary 4.2.4: bounded martingale-difference concentration
contents.reason: The conditional exponential-moment iteration and Chernoff steps are written out locally for the Doob martingale.

contents.name: Proposition 4.2.5 proof: Doob differences inherit the coordinate oscillation width
contents.reason: The source bounds conditional expectations over unrevealed coordinates by the coordinate oscillation. The local lemma supplies the measurable product-integral versions, endpoint measurability, and event-integral martingale identity for arbitrary finite products of measurable spaces.
